sam_runtime: heads-up — after the weekend kernel + quant profile rollout i'm seeing a sharp drop in prompt-priming cache hit rates for a handful of models. small/latency-sensitive requests are worst (hit ~92% -> ~65%).

liz_perf: can you paste the numbers by model and region? are these new model variants only or everything on the nodepool?

sam_runtime: quick snapshot:
```
model            old_hit    new_hit    tail_p95_ms
redwood-7b-std   0.92       0.66       78 -> 132
redwood-7b-q8    0.91       0.63       85 -> 148
redwood-13b-hyb  0.94       0.87       120 -> 140
```
this is across three AZs, but more pronounced on the opt-in canary pools where we flipped fused-matmul-tiling + quant-profile-B last saturday.

jonah: did we change any cache key canonicalization recently? i remember we adjusted ordering for kernel tiling heuristics which also touched token-run metadata serialization. could be a key tie-breaking difference.

mika: short version: quant-profile-B changed the post-embedding FP rounding and we also shipped a change that included `executor_variant` in the cache key for better routing. small numerical diffs in tokenization/kv fingerprints + new key field -> miss.

deploy-bot: compile-service: rolled out commit 9f7a3e -> fused-matmul-tiling + quant-profile-B to canary pool at 2026-03-15T03:12Z.

tina_sre: seeing p95 latency increase and a corresponding spike in L1 cache evictions on canary hosts. p95 correlates with miss rate in the priming cache. logs: 
```
[2026-03-15T03:18Z] host-a: priming_cache.misses=1223 priming_cache.hits=2350 evictions=98
[2026-03-15T03:19Z] host-b: priming_cache.misses=1980 priming_cache.hits=3200 evictions=240
```

nilesh: probable root cause: we now include `executor_variant` + an unsigned 64-bit sequence salt that gets computed from an intermediate matmul ordering value. the salt is non-deterministic across the old vs new kernel path. simplest approach: normalize salt derivation to be deterministic across kernels or remove transient fields from the key.

ashley_research: repro steps i used:
```bash
# replay the same trace against old/new binaries to compare cache key hashes
replay-trace --model redwood-7b-std --trace traces/interactive-2026-03-10.json --bin /releases/9f7a2/bin \
replay-trace --model redwood-7b-std --trace traces/interactive-2026-03-10.json --bin /releases/9f7a3/bin \
# diff produced ~1.4% of keys mismatched, most had tiny tokenization/fp-order diffs
```

mika: for a quick mitigation we can: 1) canonicalize key fields (strip executor_variant for now), 2) add a compatibility hashing layer: fallback to "loose-match" that ignores last-n bits of fingerprint for 10% of cache lookups for 24h, 3) add a deterministic salting step.

jonah: +1 to canonicalize. i'd rather we don't add loose-match unless we measure false-positive acceptance. a safer canary is: roll a small percentage (5-10%) of traffic to a compatibility path that does both strict and fallback lookup and record what would have hit. no writes on fallback.

sam_runtime: agree. can we do a fast shim that drops executor_variant out of the key for the canary pool and run compatibility lookups (read-only) for 24h? we want to measure what hit-rate would have been.

liz_perf: i'll assemble the canary plan. metrics to watch: priming_cache.hit_rate, priming_cache.evictions, p95_latency_infer, and errors. quick promqls: 
`sum(rate(priming_cache_hits[5m])) / sum(rate(priming_cache_hits[5m]) + rate(priming_cache_misses[5m]))` 
`sum(rate(priming_cache_evictions[5m]))`

tina_sre: also watch memory pressure on the nodes — fallback reads might increase CPU if we do additional hash ops. set alert if node_cpu > 75% sustained.

nilesh: patch sketch (canary only):
```diff
- key_fields = [model_id, tokenizer_fp, executor_variant, seed_salt]
+ key_fields = [model_id, tokenizer_fp, seed_salt]  # drop executor_variant for compatibility
+ // add deterministic salt: salt = md5(model_id + tokenizer_fp)[:8]
```
we'll log a histogram of "compatibility_delta" (1 if compat lookup would've hit, 0 otherwise).

ashley_research: i'll run 10k synthetic requests against both bins and produce a compatibility report. will post results here in ~2h.

sam_runtime: thanks — assigning to @liz_perf and @mika to coordinate rollout and patch. i'll hold wide rollout until we validate. :thumbsup:

jonah: follow-up action: next week we should add a cache-key audit test to CI that runs a deterministic seed through all kernel/quant permutations and ensures key equality or logs intended deltas.

sam_runtime: agreed. tagging this thread for postmortem if compat check fails.

liz_perf: updating the incident board with the canary plan and expected rollback triggers. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: canary-shim deployed to pool canary-tiling-1 at 2026-03-15T04:05Z (read-only compatibility enabled).

sam_runtime: great — i'll monitor the charts. thanks everyone. :rocket:
